title: India and Canada Push Trade Pact Talks Toward a December Conclusion Target
excerpt: Canadian trade minister Maninder Sidhu is due in New Delhi next week for a sixth round of CEPA negotiations, barely a month after the Ottawa round, as both sides try to conclude the pact ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's proposed December 11-12 visit to Canada.
body:
• India and Canada are accelerating negotiations on their proposed Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), with a sixth round due in New Delhi next week.
  • The issues under negotiation include predictable market access for Canadian pulses, greater access for services, and more visas for Indian workers and students, according to sources cited by The Hindu BusinessLine.
  • Both sides are seeking to conclude the pact ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's proposed visit to Toronto and Ottawa on December 11-12.
  • The two countries aim to more than double two-way trade to C$70 billion a year by 2030, from C$30.4 billion in 2025, according to the Canadian government.

India and Canada are accelerating negotiations for their proposed free trade agreement, with Canadian International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu scheduled to visit New Delhi next week for the sixth round of talks on the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), barely a month after the previous round in Ottawa, The Hindu BusinessLine reported.

Both countries are seeking to conclude the pact ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's proposed visit to Toronto and Ottawa on December 11-12. "There may be another round of negotiations next month before PM Modi's visit. The idea is to announce the conclusion of the deal during the visit, following which legal vetting and formal ratification can happen," a source told the newspaper. Nothing is final: neither side has made its offers public.

What Is on the Table

The key issues the two sides are seeking to resolve include predictable market access for agricultural products, including Canadian pulses, greater access for services, and more visas for Indian workers and students, according to the BusinessLine report. The fifth round, in Ottawa from October 5 to 9, covered goods, services, investment, rules of origin, intellectual property and trade remedies.

A CEPA is a comprehensive trade agreement: beyond tariffs on goods, it covers services, investment and the rules that decide where a product originates. For the Indian diaspora in Canada, the services and mobility provisions — how easily Indian professionals and students can work in Canada — are the part of the pact with the most direct personal effect, which is why visas feature among the negotiating issues.

A Fast-Moving Restart

The current talks were officially launched in March 2026, when Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and Sidhu signed the terms of reference in New Delhi in the presence of Modi and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. The effort is a restart: Canada paused earlier talks in 2023 after bilateral ties broke down, and the two sides agreed in November 2025 to resume them.

Momentum has built through the autumn. In October, Sidhu led a trade mission of nearly 300 business delegates to India — described by the Canadian government as its largest trade mission to India in more than 30 years — which concluded with 34 commercial agreements worth close to C$300 million across aerospace, clean technology, energy, information technology and agri-food. On October 13, Modi and Carney spoke by telephone and reiterated their commitment to concluding a CEPA at the earliest opportunity.

The Target

Canada and India aim to more than double two-way goods and services trade to C$70 billion annually by 2030, up from C$30.4 billion in 2025, according to the Canadian government. Whether the December target holds depends on narrowing differences on the commercially sensitive items — farm market access on one side, services and mobility on the other — in the New Delhi round and any final round before Modi's visit.
